children: RBI weighs joining private lender's plea, exploring legal options Saloni Shukla Mumbai: Yes Bank is set to file a review petition in the Supreme Court against the apex court's judgment upholding the Bombay High Court order that set aside the write-down of 8,415 crore of Additional Tier-1 (AT1) bonds, while the Reserve Bank of India is evaluating if it wants to join the private lender to seek a review of the ruling, people familiar with the matter said.

The move would mark the next legal step for the lender after the apex court upheld the Bombay High Court judgment quashing the March 2020 write-down of the AT1 instruments issued by Yes Bank. The RBI, which had backed the write-down as part of the bank's 2020 reconstruction process, is seeking legal opinion of the matter, they said. "The bank is expected to exhaust the legal remedies available to it before taking a final call on the accounting and capital treatment of the bonds," according to a person familiar with the matter.

Both Yes Bank and RBI did not respond to a query till press time. The board of Yes Bank, which is scheduled to meet on October 17 to review its second quarter results, will deliberate on the matter. The 8,415 crore payment will impact the bank's core capital that is reflected in capital adequacy ratio and not its net profit.

In an exchange disclosure, Yes Bank said it was currently reviewing the Supreme Court order and its implications and will make suitable disclosures in due course. It added that it is "examining the judgement in detail including evaluating all available legal options and suitable actions/steps going forward." title: Yes Bank Set to File Review Petition against SC Verdict
